summary: Restore the plural group in the translation

summary: Translate the narrowly avoided killing

rationale: The waxta d-qoṭal-wa clause describes a near occurrence. The edition explicitly says Vorhin hätte er beinahe meine Schwester umgebracht. The English progressive loses beinahe and presents an actual ongoing killing.

data.turoyo: Ayriyatan ste komoḥən aġ ġarataṯṯe me ḥḏoḏe ste. U ḥa, d maṣəb i ġare du ḥreno, koqoṭele, kəmmina, w košoqəl aʕ ʕənnat, d qmərwayle ste mine, w hawxa bu šəklano koməštaʕən aḥ ḥamšo, əšto zlamatani, hul d maṣibi aʕ ʕənnatani.
data.translation: Man kann außerdem noch nach den Murmeln des anderen werfen. Wer die Murmel des anderen trifft, der "tötet" ihn, wie wir sagen, und nimmt ihm auch die Geldstücke ab, die er gewonnen hatte. Und so spielen die fünf, sechs Mann, bis sie diese Zielgeldstücke treffen.

rationale: First defining example of technical active sense 2.

summary: example for sense D2 in Infectum (94/316)

data.turoyo: Heš i naqqa d kətne aʕ ʕənnatani ʕal i arʕo, u ḥa d məqṭəl, yaʕni d mitaṣibo i ġarayḏe mu ṭaraf d ḥa m am məštaʕyone, hawo konofəq mi laystkayo w lo koqomər mede bi laystkayo.
data.translation: Wenn einer "getötet", d. h. seine Murmel von einem der Mitspieler getroffen wird, während die Zielgeldstücke noch auf der Erde stehen, so scheidet er aus dem Spiel aus und kann in diesem spiele nichts mehr gewinnen.

rationale: First defining example of technical Detransitive sense D2.

summary: example for sense 1 in ko-Preterit (66/326)

data.translation: "Mein Emir, wir können ihn nicht töten. Wenn wir ihn heute töten, so kommt Morgen Kara Tadschdin aus der fremde nach Hause, und dann haben wir seinen Freund getötet. Dann wird er unbedingt auch uns töten und uns den Garaus machen.

rationale: Fills cumulative ko-Preterit 1 from three to four; completed killing assessed from a future return point.

data.translation: Der Schultheiß verstand; es tropfte ihm ins Herz: Mag sein, was will, er und der Pfarrer sind zusammen gegangen. Der Pfarrer ist habgierig; er hat ihn umgebracht.

summary: Routine counts strongly favour ordinary killing: 829 I Preterit and 648 I Infectum, compared with 10 III Preterit and 19 III Infectum. Counts are supplied aggregates, not additional reviewed occurrences.
Active reciprocity uses ḥḏoḏe or partitive mə ḥḏoḏe; agents can be l-marked, while human and animal patients are often zero-marked. qaṭlayḏux/qaṭlaṯxu encode the patient as a nominal possessor.

The existing Nomen Actionis box already distinguishes 1 killing/murder from 2 death by killing. Its inherited Detransitive placement is not morphological voice; all proposed Infinitiv innovations in this batch are refiled there.

Finite Detransitive suppresses the agent and occurs in event reports, obligations and counterfactuals. Bare qṭil and copular qṭilo-yo must remain distinct; number levelling before quantified patients already has a parallel in the inherited hundred-person example.

Preterit-wa occurs with -wa before or after the l-agent suffix. Infectum-wa covers both counterfactual outcomes and actual habitual/distributive killing; living-sufferer Preterit in 1b expresses a current result.

Do not move the existing Imperativ example merely because its narrative sequel includes Preterit qṭəlle. Initial qṭal supplies the intended Imperativ evidence. Alternate PrS verse references are not established corrections to edition page/line references.
Batch 2 preserves every earlier sense label, example and idiom. It broadens proposed 1b to explicit fright and appends technical 2 and D2, supported by the rules of the marbles game at 94/315-316.

Nominal patient possessors recur with l- after purposes/judgements, b- after commands, and m- in source/comparison phrases. These are Nomen Actionis contexts already recognized by the original entry, not newly discovered Infinitiv boxes.
At 91/51 koqṭilina is a mistaken attributed result, not an actual killing asserted by the narrator. It remains in Detransitive Preterit under the entry's existing ko-prefixed filing policy.

The reported death of a surviving story character need not establish a lexical 'disable' sense: 29/232 and 99/89-94 remain questions about narrative viewpoint. The giant's first-person living complaint at 69/196 joins the already supported hyperbolic pattern.
qṭile ruḥe bu mḥoyo at 112/55 does not securely establish self-beating syntax. The following qṭəllalli with overt town-boy agents clearly supports severe beating under 1b.

The Jan material includes interview dialogue and editorial prose; it is not uniformly a learned literary register. Historical k-Infectum reports actual killing, while gəd and conditional clauses mark threats, projected results and counterfactuals.
Nomen Actionis already has nominal senses 1 killing/murder and 2 death by killing, both filled to five after round one. Reader Infinitiv proposals do not establish a new box.

III Preterit-wa is absent from the original and round-one inventory; maqṭewole supplies it. III also permits institutional and nonintentional causation; direct versus commissioned agency is not recoverable from English killed alone.
Patient-context qṭəlle and reduced qṭəlwo recur; preserve spelling and keep exact inflection provisional. In 976 immediate Qṭil supports one explicitly qualified -wa quotation.

Existing Imperativ examples are not moved merely because narrative qṭəlle occurs in their sequel; round one already rejected that apparent entry issue. No new idiom is proposed, so an idiom search is unnecessary.
Verify qatil (JTM 5.2/98) as an Arabic lexical noun versus a native Part act. variant, and qaṭəl-/qṭiloye against qaṭolo/qṭile.
Resolve lu qṭilo (JTM 5.2/69), maqṭəl? (5.2/71), reduced maqṭeli (MAC Xalaf/71), qəṭloli (PrS 24/45), and bare Qṭəl (PrS 63/68) before treating them as secure paradigm contrasts.
Does MAC Farida/89 qṭilalle entail death in that event or severe beating? This token is withheld. Are the false cries at Mem and Zin/42 and PrS 60/71 conventional hyperbole?
PrS 62/101 has the wrong German verse; align before quotation. MAC Fingan/12 omits six were killed in the first clause; the complete following clause is used as the safe comparison.
Check JL 15.6/17 qṭalli versus inherited qṭāləli and Hors 3/17 -le versus translated mich; preserve source forms until resolved.
Confirm the source values of G̊ʶ/kʶ and emphatic person ṭ (MAC Mar Dumet/14,17), and whether casualty qṭīl is invariant or collectively construed.
Align 111/101: the supplied German describes drawing a sword against Hatim and is not the Turoyo dialogue about three brothers. No quotation from that translation is published.
Is qṭile ruḥe bu mḥoyo at 112/55 reflexive self-beating, a person-result predicate, or another construction? The idiom proposal is withheld.
Do 29/232 and 99/89-94 report presumed death or use conventional nonfatal qṭl? Their supplied verses do not independently settle the prior survival history.
Confirm qoṭule at 91/34 and Arabic-shaped qatəl at Talay 1/114 before treating either as a systematic local Part act. variant.
Check contracted qoṭanna at 113/231 against the third-person narrative, and gqəṭlile at 95/168 against the first-person patient translation; no silent normalization.
Check patient-context qṭəlle at 1.8/138,140,171 and 1.46/1981: indefinite-agent active, dialect Detransitive or source irregularity?
Resolve l-agent/victim coding in maqṭalle (1.19/933), maqṭela/maqṭewola (1.23/1195,1197) and maqṭəlulle/maqṭələnne (1204,1207).
Are qatəl/Qaṭəl (1.8/170, 2.2/42, 2.4/569, 2.18/3732) Arabic nouns or native Part act. variants? Establish the root/stem of mtaqtəli (3.1/19) before adding II.

Check qṭəlno (1.45/1950), quṯewole (1967), qṭiwolən (1.53/2568), quṭewolən (2.4/731), qəṭlile (2.16/3558), kqəṭliwole (1.54/2612), gədquṭewolle (2.18/3742), and qṭəlallen/qṭəlalan (3743); do not infer spelling repairs from English.

summary: Money and a decree may be metonymic causes of killing; their grammatical-subject status is not equally secure. Wealth alone does not establish figurative ruin.
Plant patients include weed eradication and personified wheat/pomegranate in riddles. Do not lexicalize milling or opening from the riddle solution.
Town names stand for their inhabitants; no demolition sense. The Arabic quotation at PrS 10/73 is excluded from native morphology.
Reflexive ruḥ- with an active causative gives letting oneself be killed; it is not a Detransitive form or an independent sense.
Living mounts exhausted or battered during prolonged fighting extend the same nonfatal-affliction reading to animal patients; no new numbered sense.
ʕal u rabo in 30/169 may specify the weapon's target rather than qṭl government; do not establish a special prepositional sense.
Plane crashes extend caused death beyond intentional murder; no independent died sense.
Supports round-one affliction and extends it to self-exhaustion at work. Duration in 584 is direct evidence; later survival is not independently supplied.
Suicide question extends the round-one reflexive victim pattern, without proving a distinct direct-killing lexical sense.
ʕal iḏe agent phrases occur in historical Infectum and Preterit; qṭil with numeral/partitive patients continues round-one number observations.
